newsitem.title: USA: Texas regulators lobby for oil, gas tax incentives.
newsitem.headline: Texas regulators lobby for oil, gas tax incentives.

text.p: The Texas Railroad Commission plans to lobby to revive a tax incentive program for marginal oil and gas wells in the state, commission Chairman Charles Matthews said in an interview this week.
The commission, which regulates Texas oil and gas production, will encourage Texas lawmakers to give operators of marginal oil and gas wells brought back on line a break from state severance taxes.

An estimated 3,800 wells were back into production following passage of a similar tax break in 1993, but a push to renew the legislation was caught up up last minute parliamentary wrangling in 1995 and the program expired.
Revenue lost from the tax break was offset by $29 million in sales taxes from increased employment and spending on well equipment and services, according to the commission.
Matthews was elected as chairman of the three-member commission on Jan. 7.
